page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Built on KVM hypervisor technology, it features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. The system includes 16.0 GB of RAM, offering 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU core. It has 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 extensions. The instance includes 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local SSD storage, and no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In synthetic benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates mixed performance across compute and memory workloads. Single-core processing yields moderate results, achieving an average Geekbench single-core score of 1282.0, a PassMark encryption score of 4224.57, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 9.2 GB/sec. Multi-core and heavy compute benchmarks show lower relative scaling, with stress-ng single-core (762.69) and multi-core (1531.17) scores falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth achieves 31.83 GB/sec for large block reads and 16.28 GB/sec for large block writes. Application-level metrics show Redis SET throughput reaching 3.6 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measuring 3.96 GB/sec.

Given its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g6a.xlarge provides entry-level general resource capacity. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached network storage for all persistent data requirements. The hardware configuration makes this server instance best suited for general application backends, basic web serving, staging environments, and lightweight microservices that do not require intense parallel compute or high disk input/output.

The CPU features 16 MB of L3 cache along with hardware acceleration for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, while omitting AVX-512 capabilities. Local storage is absent, requiring attached cloud storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.
